note: The field-shape CONTRACT: the one place the vault's metadata shape rules are written down. Everything else is loaded or generated from this file and pinned to it by tests — Prism's write guard and lint (apps/server/src/vault-shapes.ts, worker/vault-lint.ts), the agent repo's guard (scripts/vault_shapes.py, which carries a byte-identical vendored copy at config/vault-shapes.json), and the 'Field shapes' block in every routine / agent prompt (docs/vault-field-shapes.md, rendered by renderFieldShapesBlock). It must agree with tag-schemas.json and scripts/vault-hygiene/schema-fixes.json (apps/server/test/schema-drift.test.ts fails otherwise). To change a shape: docs/vault-schema-change.md.

undeclaredListFields._note: List fields the writers produce that no tag schema declares yet (so the vault does not validate them; the guard and lint still do). Declaring one = a schema change.

exemptArrayFields._note: Declared array fields the guard deliberately leaves alone.

email.labels: ingest-owned: worker/proton.ts and worker/gmail.ts always write an array; no other writer may touch it

exemptTags._note: Schema'd tags outside the personal-vault contract. Prefix match when the name ends with '*'.
exemptTags.governance-*: metadata is HMAC-signed (governance-integrity.ts); never rewritten by a guard
exemptTags.entity: bioregional commons schema (not seeded in the personal vault)

prompt.heading: ## Field shapes (bind hard — every note you create or update)
prompt.intro: The vault validates these shapes; a wrong one is a warning on that note forever and breaks Prism's database views. This block is generated from the approved schema (Prism `packages/core/src/lib/schemas/vault-shapes.json`); the write guards and the daily vault lint enforce the same rules.
rules: LIST fields are lists, and an empty list is ABSENT: never write `""` (or `" "`, or `[""]`) to a list field. Nothing to say → leave the key out; to clear a list, write `[]`. One value is still a list: `["[[…]]"]`. The list fields — {listFieldsByTag}.
No empty scalars either: omit a field you have no value for (`source`, `role`, `contact`, `confidence`, `due`, …) instead of writing `""`.

Project links point at the project NOTE, never the folder: `[[{projectFolder}/<slug>/{projectNote}]]`. `[[{projectFolder}/<slug>]]` resolves to nothing. Only link a project slug that already has that note (query-notes { id: "{projectFolder}/<slug>/{projectNote}" }); otherwise mention it in prose.
People links point at an EXISTING person note path you looked up; never invent `[[vault/people/<Title Name>]]`.

Keep what you write linked: a meeting, transcript, briefing or research note names its people and projects in the list fields above (`attendees` / `people` / `projects`) as links to those existing notes — that is what keeps the vault connected.
`confidence` on {confidenceTags} is a label: {confidenceLabels} (never a number).
Task `status` (only when you touch an existing task): {agentTaskStatuses} ({mirrorTaskStatuses} only on ClickUp mirrors). Status lives in metadata, never as a tag.
{sourceTags} `source`: one lower-case word — {sources}; leave an existing `source` exactly as it is.

`recording_id` is text (`"12345"`, quoted), never a number. Spec `version` is text too (`"1.2"`). `lastMessageAt` on message threads is epoch milliseconds (an integer) — and is owned by the ingester: do not write it.
